turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict each
candidate's largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, then select the 5
candidates whose |d_ij| is CLOSEST to 20 pm/V.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The SHG tensor vanishes by symmetry in any centrosymmetric crystal, so only non-centrosymmetric candidates can produce a finite \(|d_{ij}|\). Inspection of the supplied POSCARs immediately identifies the six SiC polytypes (c024–c029) as the classic non-centrosymmetric tetrahedral semiconductors 3C (\(F\bar{4}3m\)), 2H (\(P6_3mc\)), 4H, 6H, 8H and 15R.  

For these polytypes the bond-charge/Levine model together with the known refractive indices (\(n\approx2.55\)–2.65) and the measured/calculated literature values give  
\[
|d_{14}(3C)|\approx18\text{–}21\,\text{pm/V},\qquad
|d_{33}(2H)|\approx17\text{–}19\,\text{pm/V},
\]
with the longer-period hexagonal and rhombohedral polytypes falling in the same 12–18 pm/V window because their hexagonality (net alignment of Si–C bilayers) remains high. All six numbers therefore lie within a few pm/V of the target value 20 pm/V.  

All other chemistries in the pool are either centrosymmetric (\(|d|=0\)) or, when polar, possess substantially different number densities of polarizable bonds, different alignment factors or different band gaps, pushing their largest \(|d_{ij}|\) well below 10 pm/V or well above 30 pm/V. Consequently the five SiC entries closest to 20 pm/V (cubic 3C first, then the highest-hexagonality hexagonal polytypes) are c027, c025, c026, c028 and c029.

Final: c027, c025, c026, c028, c029
